Vaemond furiously snaps that Viserys has no right to decide House Velaryon's fate, and rages that he will not allow the end of House Velaryon on the account of Lucerys, holding his tongue before openly calling the boy a bastard. Challenged by Daemon to continue, Vaemond screams that Rhaenyra's children are bastards and that she is a whore. Viserys vows to take his tongue for the insult against his daughter, but Daemon promptly executes Vaemond before Viserys gets the chance. Rhaenyra then approaches her father as he collapses in pain on the throne, pleading him to take medical assistance alongside Alicent. Rhaenyra dines with her family. Later that night, Rhaenyra and Daemon's family join Viserys and Alicent's family for a supper, commemorating Luke's succession to Driftmark and the betrothals of Jace and Baela, and Luke and Rhaena. Viserys makes a despondent speech about the fragmented state of House Targaryen that has worsened over the last 20 years, and begs Rhaenyra and Alicent's families to make peace for him. Rhaenyra proceeds to thank Alicent for her years of servitude to the king and for taking care of her father for all these years when she could not. She also apologizes for the strife she may have caused Alicent and Viserys since being named Princess of Dragonstone and hopes for an end to the infighting. Alicent then thanks Rhaenyra for her sentiment, stating they are both mothers, and they may have more in common than they sometimes allow. She then toasts Rhaenyra, stating she will make a fine queen. The supper then starts, with the Targaryen family in a state of happiness and peace for the first time in 20 years. Viserys is then taken from the room during a sudden onset of extreme pain. A fight then ensues after Aemond makes a passively aggressive tribute to Jace, Luke, and Joff, calling them " strong " in reference to their real father's family. Rhaenyra then orders her sons to her bedchambers, and declares her intention to return to Dragonstone. Alicent states that Rhaenyra has only just arrived, and wishes for her to stay, prompting Rhaenyra to say she will return on dragonback after escorting the children home, to Alicent's delight. After Rhaenyra and her family return to Dragonstone, Viserys passes away, succumbing to his illnesses, after mistaking Alicent for Rhaenyra and telling her that he believes her to be the Prince That Was Promised, and she will be the one to unite the realm, which Alicent misinterprets as Viserys wanting Aegon to succeed him as king. A coup is then staged in King's Landing, which results in Aegon being crowned King of the Andals and the Rhoynar and the First Men, displacing Rhaenyra. Rhaenyra talks to Luke about Driftmark. On Dragonstone, Rhaenyra finds Luke studying the island of Driftmark on the Painted Table of Dragonstone. Luke insists that he doesn't want Driftmark, and that the lordship should have passed to Ser Vaemond. Rhaenyra assures her son that she felt the same when her father Viserys named her Princess of Dragonstone, and promises that just as Viserys prepared her to play that part, she will do the same for him. They are interrupted by Ser Lorent Marbrand of the Kingsguard, who informs Rhaenyra that Princess Rhaenys has arrived on dragonback, and requests an audience with her and Prince Daemon. Rhaenyra welcomes Rhaenys to Dragonstone, and asks if there is word of her husband Lord Corlys's recovery, but Rhaenys interrupts to inform Rhaenyra and Daemon that Viserys is dead. Daemon inquires how Viserys died, to which Rhaenys replies that she does not know. Daemon then draws the conclusion that Viserys has been murdered by Alicent and Otto. Rhaenys also informs them that the Greens have usurped King's Landing, and Aegon has been crowned as Viserys's successor. Rhaenyra is appalled to learn that Aegon had been crowned before the masses, knowing, as Rhaenys reiterates, that the masses will now see Aegon as the true king. Rhaenys advises Rhaenyra to leave Dragonstone with her family at once, before the Greens come for her. Rhaenyra then doubles over in pain, reaching beneath her dress. Her fingers come away bloody, and she realized that the shock of the news has sent her into premature labor. Rhaenyra is crowned as queen. Rhaenyra struggles with her labor pains, attended by Maester Gerardys, Elinda Massey, and several midwives, all of whom are fearful as Rhaenyra's pregnancy is far from full term. Jace and Luke are summoned to Rhaenyra's bedchamber, where Rhaenyra informs them of their grandfather Viserys's death, Aegon and the Greens' usurpation of the Iron Throne, and Daemon's preparation for war. Rhaenyra then instructs Jace to control the situation with her supporters, as he is now heir to any claim Rhaenyra has left, and that nothing is to be done without her leave. Ignoring the advice of her midwives to help her, Rhaenyra gives birth to a deformed, stillborn daughter (that she planned to name Visenya ). She later prepares the child for burial under the watchful eye of the Silent Sisters . A small funeral is later held outside. The funeral is interrupted by the arrival of Ser Erryk Cargyll , who kneels before Rhaenyra and declares his loyalty to her, and offers her the crown of Viserys and Jaehaerys, stolen from the Red Keep in the confusion of the Green coup. Daemon places the crown on Rhaenyra's head, kneeling before her and declaring her his queen. Rhaenyra's sons, stepdaughters, Queensguard, and the congregation (save Rhaenys) kneel before Rhaenyra as the rightful queen of the Seven Kingdoms. Rhaenyra's attendant lords gather around the Painted Table, readying themselves for Rhaenyra's first council meeting, placing map markers on the table and lighting it up with candles, with Rhaenyra approaching, flanked by knights of House Targaryen. As Rhaenyra enters, Daemon formally announces her as "Queen Rhaenyra Targaryen, First of Her Name, Queen of the Andals and the Rhoynar and the First Men, Lady of the Seven Kingdoms and Protector of the Realm." She is offered wine by her stepdaughter, Rhaena, who she then thanks and invites to join the Black Council at the Painted Table. Rhaenyra takes a moment to contemplate her situation, before asking for a report on the Blacks ' standing. Daemon informs Rhaenyra that Dragonstone's garrison stands at 30 knights, 100 crossbowmen, and 300 men-at-arms; sufficient to defend the island, but not to conquer Westeros, and word has been sent to the loyalists within the City Watch. The loyalties of Houses Celtigar , Massey , Darklyn , Staunton , and Bar Emmon have been secured, with Rhaenyra adding that House Arryn will also declare loyalty due to their shared kinship through Rhaenyra's mother, Aemma Arryn. The loyalties of Houses Tully , Baratheon , and Stark are brought into question; whereas the Starks are staunchly loyal oathkeepers as well as the other Northern houses, who will follow where the Starks lead, Lord Borros Baratheon will need to be reminded of his late father's oath. Rhaenyra then turns her attention to Princess Rhaenys, and asks for news from Driftmark. Rhaenys says that Corlys sails for Dragonstone, though his loyalty to Rhaenyra and the Blacks is still in the air. Rhaenyra and Daemon surmise that House Lannister will not support them due to Ser Tyland Lannister 's servitude to Otto, and that with the Lannisters' allegiance to the Greens, the Westerlands will also support the Greens, so the Riverlands are essential to the Blacks' cause. Lord Bartimos Celtigar interrupts, arguing that talk of men is irrelevant, when Rhaenyra's forces command dragons in numbers not wielded since the days of Old Valyria. Rhaenyra points out that the Greens also command dragons, but Daemon points out that they only have three adult dragons, compared to the Blacks' command of Syrax, Caraxes, Meleys , Vermax , Arrax , Tyraxes , and Moondancer . He also notes that there are several unclaimed dragons in need of riders, all of whom nest in regions that the Blacks control. Daemon suggests using the dragons to lay waste to King's Landing, but before further discussion can be had, Ser Erryk interrupts to inform them a galleon is approaching Dragonstone, flying the banner of a three-headed green dragon. Rhaenyra arrives on the bridge leading to Dragonstone, atop Syrax, to confront the Green negotiation party, headed by Ser Otto Hightower. Otto greets Rhaenyra as "Princess," but Rhaenyra icily retorts that she is Queen Rhaenyra now, labeling Otto and his companions as traitors to the realm. Otto presents Aegon II's peace terms to Rhaenyra in return for Rhaenyra's allegiance and her acknowledgement of Aegon being king: Rhaenyra will keep Dragonstone, and the castle will pass to Jacaerys upon her death; Lucerys will be confirmed as the legitimate heir to Driftmark, and all the lands and holdings of House Velaryon. Rhaenyra and Daemon's sons will be given places of honor at court: Aegon the Younger as the king's squire and Viserys as his cupbearer ; and Aegon II will pardon any knight or lord who conspired against his ascent to the Iron Throne. Otto states that Aegon's claim is far more legitimate than Rhaenyra's as he was crowned by a septon of the Faith before the masses of King's Landing, and carries Aegon the Conqueror 's crown, sword , and name. Rhaenyra asserts that Houses Baratheon, Stark, and Tully all swore allegiance to her when Viserys I named her his heir, to which Otto smugly replies that stale oaths will not put Rhaenyra on the Iron Throne, and that the succession changed the day Aegon was born. Rhaenyra proceeds to rip Otto's badge of office from his cloak, denouncing him as a "fucking traitor." Otto then gives Rhaenyra a sheaf of parchment, which is revealed to be a page torn from Ten Thousand Ships , a book she and Alicent read when they were teenagers in the godswood 20 years ago. Daemon, enraged at Otto's attempts to manipulate his wife, calls to end this farce, and kill the negotiation party, but is stopped by Rhaenyra, who declares that King's Landing shall have her answer to their terms on the morrow. Rhaenyra and her advisors discuss the terms offered to them by the Greens. Rhaenyra states that she knows the histories of Valyria and the dangerous potential of dragons thanks to her father's teachings: when dragons flew to war, everything burned, and she doesn't wish to rule over a kingdom of ash and bone. Rhaenyra asserts to her advisors that it is her duty to hold the realm together, rather than descend it into war and chaos just for her pursuit of the Iron Throne. Daemon rebukes this, stating that the Greens have already declared war and raises his voice at Rhaenyra's inaction. Rhaenyra and Daemon then talk privately, with Daemon insisting that she cannot submit to the Hightowers, who have stolen her birthright, and that it is her duty as queen to crush rebellion. Rhaenyra protests that they are bound by more than personal ambition, reminding Daemon of what Viserys told them about the "Song of Ice and Fire," and Aegon the Conqueror's goal to keep the realm united against the coming great evil in the north, only for Daemon to seize her by the throat. Daemon angrily hisses that Viserys was obsessed with omens and prophecies to give meaning to his feckless reign and that dragons, not dreams, made the Targaryens kings. Daemon then releases Rhaenyra, who is taken aback by his violence against her, but quickly comes to the realization that Viserys never told Daemon about Aegon's dream, indicating Viserys never once truly viewed Daemon as his heir. Corlys Velaryon pledges allegiance to Rhaenyra. The next morning, Rhaenyra heads another congregation of the Black Council, which Corlys, who has finally arrived at Dragonstone, attends with his wife Rhaenys, and his granddaughters Baela and Rhaena. Rhaenyra quickly expresses her relief to see Corlys healthy again, while Corlys offers her condolences for Viserys's death. He points out that Rhaenyra has too few allies to win a war for the throne, and that the hope of allies from Houses Stark, Arryn, and Baratheon is potentially futile. Rhaenyra point out that all the noble houses of the realm swore fealty to her when Viserys named her heir, and when Corlys points out that House Hightower too swore their allegiance, Corlys and House Velaryon also did. Corlys notes that his and Rhaenyra's are bound by common blood and common cause, and declares his allegiance to Rhaenyra and the Blacks. Rhaenyra thanks him and Rhaenys for their support, but insists that if war's first stroke is to fall it will not be by her hand, as she wishes to know who her allies are before sending them to war. Corlys adds that House Velaryon now controls the Stepstones, as the Triarchy have been routed from the region, and they have been properly garrisoned this time. He states his men will institute a blockade of the shipping lanes that pass through the Stepstones, and that a second blockade will be placed across the Gullet , reinforced by Rhaenys and Meleys, to cut off all sea trade to King's Landing. This would aim to starve the Greens into surrender, but Rhaenyra asserts they need to secure the allegiance of the Starks, Arryns, and Baratheons before having enough men to surround King's Landing. Jace suggests that he and Luke bear Rhaenyra's messages themselves on dragonback, as dragons are faster than ravens, and will be intimidating and therefore more persuasive to the lords of Westeros. Corlys agrees, and Rhaenyra decides that Jace will go the Eyrie and then to Winterfell to win the support of Lady Jeyne Arryn and Lord Cregan Stark , while Luke will travel south to Storm's End to ensure the support of Lord Borros Baratheon. That evening, Rhaenyra speaks with Jace and Luke before they depart on their mission. Rhaenyra notes that while some may view the Targaryens as closer to gods than to men, if they wish to rule Westeros, the Targaryens must answer to the gods of Westeros. Appalled by her error, a sobbing Rhaenyra pulls Dark Sister free and beheads Otto with her second stroke. Daemon takes back Dark Sister from her and beheads Jasper for his treason. Rhaenyra steps through Otto's blood, ascends the steps to the Iron Throne, and seats herself upon it as a captured Alicent and Helaena are brought into the throne room. Alicent glances in horror at the sight of her father's decapitated body, immediately realizing that Rhaenyra had executed him, and stares at Rhaenyra, who glares back at her. Rhaenyra dispatches Daemon, Hugh, Ulf, and their respective dragons to compel Lord Ormund Hightower to bend the knee to her and surrender his ward, her youngest half-brother Prince Daeron Targaryen to Black custody, though she forbids Daemon from simply slaughtering the lot of them with Caraxes as he desired. Upon Daemon's return to King's Landing and meeting her youngest half-brother for the first time, Rhaenyra interrogates Daeron as to Ormund's knowledge of the Greens' plot to crown Aegon over her, and Aegon and Aemond's wherabouts. When Daeron refuses to answer, she orders him imprisoned. Daemon advocates executing him (since as an heir to both Viserys and Aegon, Daeron will always be a threat to her), but Rhaenyra is reluctant to kill the boy. Rhaenyra and Daemon head to the Small Council chamber to find Lord Corlys Velaryon and Mysaria (both having arrived at court in the intervening days since the city's fall) interrogating Grand Maester Orwyle about the location of the royal treasury's contents. Orwyle explains that Tyland Lannister in his capacity as Master of Coin spoke of dividing the crown's gold and moving it out of the city, though Orwyle insists he doesn't know where, as the rest of the Green Council didn't trust him enough to share their plans. When Rhaenyra presses him, Orwyle insists that other than Tyland (presumed dead at the Battle of the Gullet), the only other person who might have known would be Jasper Wylde (whom Daemon executed for treason). Rhaenyra asks both Mysaria and Corlys for their opinion; both concede they believe Orwyle is telling the truth. Daemon scoffs at Mysaria, but Rhaenyra speaks up in defense of her Mistress of Whisperers . Rhaenyra insists she must have a formal coronation to give legitimacy to her reign, but Mysaria advises against such a grandiose, expensive spectacle when most of the city's people are still starving. Corlys and Mysaria also warn Rhaenyra that the survivors of the Triarchy fleet from the Gullet are now attacking villages along the coastline, the city's granaries are nearly empty and the effects of the war make it still too dangerous for farmers to sow crops or trade routes to reopen. Rhaenyra commands Orwyle to send a raven to Casterly Rock in the hopes Tyland hid the gold there, and ravens to loyal lords across the realm demanding tribute for their queen. Corlys asks if Rhaenyra will summon the rest of the Black Council from Dragonstone but Rhaenyra insists, after their indirect betrayal of her alongside Jace, she has no further use for them. Rhaenyra asks of Aemond's whereabouts. Orwyle informs her that he and Vhagar destroyed the garrison Daemon left at Harrenhal and slew its castellan, Ser Simon Strong along with his sons. Rhaenyra orders Baela and Moondancer to scout for any signs of Aemond or Sheepstealer, pledging to grant Harrenhal to whomever slays Aemond for her. She rises and moves to leave the chamber, only to start in shock and disgust as she nearly treads on a rat. Orwyle explains that, due to Aegon II executing the Red Keep's complement of ratcatchers after the murder of his son, the castle is overrun with the vermin. Rhaenyra interrogates Alicent. Rhaenyra walks with Ser Luthor Largent as her sworn shield. While Luthor insists it is an honor, he urges Rhaenyra to select new Queensguard members so that he might return to his duties as Commander of the City Watch. Luthor fends off enquiries from members of the Red Keep's household staff asking what the Queen wishes done to resolve one problem or another as Rhaenyra heads to the royal apartments where Alicent and Helaena are being held in genteel imprisonment. Rhaenyra demands to know where the contents of the treasury are, but Alicent insists she doesn't know either; the Green Council, up to and including her own father, never saw fit to share their schemes with her. Rhaenyra scoffs at this, to which Alicent retorts she would advise Rhaenyra to question Otto himself had she not had him unceremoniously executed. Helaena gently asks her half-sister if executing Otto made Rhaenyra feel better about losing Jace. Rhaenyra retorts that she would have preferred to execute Aegon instead, and indirectly accuses Alicent and Helaena of having helped him escape the city. Both women insist they don't know how Aegon escaped, Alicent pinning the blame on Larys, and denying any knowledge of where Aemond is or Sheepstealer's new rider when Rhaenyra angrily presses them for details. Alicent points out she fulfilled her end of the bargain she negotiated with Rhaenyra when she came to Dragonstone to the best of her ability, yet Rhaenyra is still holding them prisoner. Rhaenyra insists she cannot release them until Aegon and Aemond have been dealt with, but promises they won't be harmed. They will be fed and clothed, allowed to visit the castle's godswood , and she will allow Jaehaera (who has been separated from her mother and grandmother) to spend time with them. Alicent is displeased, but Rhaenyra makes clear the matter is not up for debate. Rhaenyra speaks next with Mysaria, commanding her to spread word that Aegon was found dead when the Blacks took King's Landing, and to summon her now eldest son and heir Joffrey back from the Vale of Arryn. She discusses her half-brother Daeron with Mysaria. Like Daemon, Mysaria agrees Daeron is a threat to her rule and the best course of action would be to execute him. Rhaenyra is initially reluctant, as Daeron has not committed the same crimes against her that Aegon and Aemond have, but when she sees what appears to be Jace walking towards her, she briefly contemplates having Daeron executed to spitefully take a son from Alicent, since she has lost two. Putting the matter aside, Rhaenyra asks Mysaria to bring Elinda Massey from the city into the castle to resume her duties as Rhaenyra's lady-in-waiting, and to interrogate the castle staff and replace any still loyal to the Hightowers. Rhaenyra meets the High Septon. Rhaenyra meets next with the High Septon in the throne room. While expenses prevent her from holding a coronation, she presses the High Septon to formally annoint her as Queen, so the people of Westeros can see her rule is blessed by the Faith of the Seven . When Rhaenyra informs him Aegon is dead, the High Septon questions why his body has not been shown, nor the Silent Sisters summoned to perform the proper funerary rights. Rhaenyra argues that her ascent to the throne and Aegon's downfall could not have happened were it not the will of the Seven , but the High Septon dismisses her claims of dragons being proof of the Seven's favor, calling the creatures a profane magic that can only bring about destruction. Angered by his refusal, Rhaenyra storms out of the meeting, even as the High Septon warns her it would be disastrous to make an enemy of the Faith. That evening, Rhaenyra dines with Corlys, Addam of Hull and Alyn of Hull . Corlys confesses the pair are his sons, fathered on a woman he met on his voyages before he married Princess Rhaenys. Corlys explains he kept them out of sight not to offend his wife, but he has recognized them, and wishes for Rhaenyra to formally legitimize them as his sons and members of House Velaryon , so that he might name Alyn his heir and ensure the continuation of his line. Although Rhaenyra praises both men for their loyal service to her, she demurs Corlys's request. Rhaenyra holds court in the throne room. The next day, Rhaenyra holds court in the throne room and answers petitions from the smallfolk; she agrees to allow sheep allocated to feed the dragons to be harvested of their fleeces and limited hunting in the Kingswood to alleviate the shortfalls in wool and meat. Among the petitioners is Sylvi , who asks for justice over the fact that at the start of the war, the nobility hoarded food, resulting in widespread starvation within the city. At a Small Council meeting afterwards, Rhaenyra presides over a dispute between Daemon, who argues against alienating the nobility by giving in to the complaining of the commoners, and Mysaria, who argues that ignoring the smallfolk's genuine concerns will lead to trouble. Rhaenyra interrupts their argument to ask if Baela has reported any signs of Vhagar: Daemon replies the only dragon she has seen is Sunfyre's carcass. Rhaenyra orders Addam to join the hunt, insisting Vhagar and Aemond cannot hide forever, intending to take what small measure of justice she can from those who have wronged her. When Mysaria asks what is to be done about the smallfolk's requests, Rhaenyra enigmatically answers "A banquet" . That afternoon, Rhaenyra has Addam, Hugh and Ulf knighted for their services to her, dubbing them Ser Hugh Hammer, Ser Ulf White (having flatly refused Ulf's request to be dubbed 'Targaryen') and Ser Addam of Hull (not Velaryon, to Addam's clear disappointment). After the ceremony, Hugh asks Rhaenyra about the accomodations she promised for him and his wife (who has since left him and gone to live with her family in Tumbleton ): Rhaenyra promises to deal with the matter once her current affairs are in order. She is also visited by Alicent, who requests Rhaenyra send Otto's body to Oldtown so he can be buried alongside her mother , a request Rhaenyra grants. Despite the awkwardness, the pair briefly commiserate over the pressures of ruling a kingdom, with Alicent warning Rhaenyra she will end up doing things that go against her conscience and her beliefs before she took the crown in order to rule: Rhaenyra disputes this, insisting her father wasn't changed by the crown, but Alicent counters that Viserys lived in his own little world as king, and neither of them truly knew him outside of it. That evening, Rhaenyra presides over a banquet for the nobility of King's Landing, rebuking them with thinly veiled courtesy for their passivity in resisting the Hightowers' usurpation of the throne from her, before serving them some of the rats infesting the Red Keep caught and roasted, and lambasting them for hoarding food while the smallfolk starved. The gathered nobles try to defend their actions as concern for their families, but Rhaenyra castigates them for treating the smallfolk's concern for such as any lesser, before informing them the gold cloaks are currently raiding their storehouses and seizing what they have hoarded to redistribute to the people. The nobles protest she is robbing them, but Rhaenyra retorts she is merely reminding them of their duty to the crown. As she leaves, she is approached by Ser Torrhen Manderly , who amusedly compliments her actions, commenting that it might appease the smallfolk enough to forget that it was on her orders the Velaryon fleet imposed the blockade that caused widespread starvation in the first place, much to her annoyance at his flippant attitude. Afterwards, in the Red Keep's courtyard, Daemon warns Rhaenyra her actions will anger the nobility and provide only a temporary respite for the smallfolk's problems: Rhaenyra agrees, and dispatches Daemon to the Eyrie to demand Lady Jeyne Arryn pay in gold to compensate for failing to contribute soldiers to the Blacks' war effort. Daemon attempts to console his wife over her uncertainty in ruling, urging her that they launch military campaigns to conquer Dorne , the Free Cities and even Yi Ti to create an empire their children can rule over for eternity. Rhaenyra insists they need to win their current war first, to which Daemon remind her she will need to kill Daeron sooner or later before he departs. Rhaenyra winning over the smallfolk. The next day, Rhaenyra, with Mysaria's aid, distributes food confiscated from the nobility to a cheering crowd of smallfolk outside the Grand Sept . Upon her return to the Red Keep, however, she is accosted by Corlys Velaryon, who demands an explanation why she refused to legitimize Addam and Alyn. Rhaenyra insists at this early stage in her reign, she cannot be seen to be legitimizing bastards, given the rumors around her own children's paternity, but Corlys, angered at Rhaenyra denying him his sole request after all the sacrifices he has made for her cause, angrily brands Jace, Luke and Joffrey bastards and demands she tell him why she sees fit to deny his children the legitimacy she granted hers. Ser Luthor Largent rebukes Corlys for his outburst, but Rhaenyra is reduced to stunned silence. Later that day, Rhaenyra informs Alicent her youngest son Daeron is a prisoner in the Red Keep. Alicent asks what she will do with him: Rhaenyra says that she is within her rights to have Daeron executed, but since his crimes against her are far less than those of Aegon and Aemond, she will settle for simply banishing him to the Night's Watch . Alicent, who last saw Daeron when he was five before he was sent to be Ormund's ward in Oldtown, requests that she be allowed to say goodbye to Daeron before he is sent to Castle Black : Rhaenyra agrees and arranges the meeting, but when Alicent shows no sign of recognition, she realizes the boy Ormund gave Daemon is not Daeron. The imposter Daeron confesses he is a merchant's son from Tumbleton, who Ormund forced to go along with his deceit under threat of executing the boy's mother. A furious Rhaenyra demands to know what Ormund is playing at, as he had to know she would uncover the deception sooner or later. She gets her answer that evening: as she presides over a bonfire of Hightower banners and drapery torn down following her capture of King's Landing, a wounded Dragonkeeper arrives and informs her Ormund's army has conquered Tumbleton, in hopes of goading her to destroy a Black stronghold to root him out and turn Westeros against her through her willingness to kill her loyal subjects. The next day, Rhaenyra presides over a meeting of the Small Council (though Corlys absents himself) to discuss Ormund Hightower's conquest of Tumbleton: Rhaenyra notes that the town is not a formidable stronghold, but speculates that, by holding it, Ormund is trying to bait her into destroying a town that raised her banner and is populated by hundreds of her loyal subjects, which in the eyes of the rest of Westeros would make her a monster as vile as Maegor the Cruel . Orwyle speaks up, proposing Rhaenyra command Lords Oscar Tully and Roderick Dustin , whose army is still marching to King's Landing from the Riverlands , to divert their march to Tumbleton instead. Mysaria agrees with the suggestion, noting that while the fighting to drive Ormund and his army from Tumbleton will still be bloody, using the Riverlanders and Winter Wolves will be far less destructive than dragon riders. Rhaenyra consents, instructing Orwyle to send a raven to Lord Tully with his new orders, as well as offering Orwyle back his position as Grand Maester and his seat on the Small Council, provided he serve her loyally and inform Mysaria of where and whom he dispatches all his ravens to. She also commands a dragon and rider be sent to watch Tumbleton, ensuring Ormund and his army cannot leave the town without being seen. When the proceedings turn to discuss the crown's dire finances, Mysaria advises Rhaenyra to name a new Master of Coin , with the intent of scapegoating him when the smallfolk learn how badly short of resources the city is. Rhaenyra agrees, instructing Mysaria to make enquires as to Ser Torrhen Manderly 's suitability for the post. After the meeting adjourns, Rhaenyra goes to speak with Alicent in the castle godswood, trying to get more information about Ormund. Alicent admits she barely knows her cousin, telling Rhaenyra that Ormund considers himself a scholar and historian, that he is reportedly fatherly towards Daeron, that Gwayne frequently complained of Ormund's cruelty when they were children, and that he apparently has a strong sensitivity to odours. Rhaenyra asks Alicent if she regretted sending Daeron to be a ward in Oldtown: Alicent insists the decision was hers, as she wanted a Hightower child after bearing three Targaryens for Viserys, and wonders if sending Daeron away was the best choice she made as a mother, sparing him from turning out like her other sons. Rhaenyra in her father's solar Later that day, Rhaenyra meets with Alyn of Hull in her father's solar: Alyn explains that Corlys has left King's Landing to hunt down the survivors of the Triarchy fleet from the Battle of the Gullet , suggesting that battle might be what his father needs to clear his head and calms tensions between him and Rhaenyra. When Alyn notices Viserys's model of Old Valyria , Rhaenyra and Alyn briefly commiserate over their struggles to escape the shadow of their fathers' legacies. She is disgusted to see the model, like the rest of the castle, is infested with rats, but intrigued when Alyn notes that the Velaryon fleet kept cats aboard their ships to deal with such rodents, clearly considering the possibility. She also meets with Hugh Hammer , who requests that he and Vermithor be sent to watch Tumbleton instead of Ulf and Silverwing , out of concern for his wife's safety. Rhaenyra consents that he and Ulf will share the watch over Tumbleton, agreeing to let Hugh go first. Rhaenyra later to Orwyle's chambers and commands him to gather any and all correspondence by raven between Otto and Ormund Hightower, and asks him how much influence House Hightower has over the Faith of the Seven . While Orwyle admits the two have long been intertwined, as the Hightowers endowed the construction of the Starry Sept and the Faith has been a presence in Oldtown since before Aegon's Conquest , he insists the Faith would never allow itself to be directly influenced by a noble house, even one as influential as the Hightowers. When Rhaenyra informs Orwyle the High Septon has refused to annoint her as queen, Orwyle questions if such a symbolic gesture matters, given Rhaenyra holds the capital, the Iron Throne and multiple dragons to showcase her power. When Rhaenyra proposes removing the High Septon, Orwyle warns her that directly stripping the High Septon of his position would likely incite the faithful to violence, and obliquely asks if she is thinking of having the High Septon assassinated. Amused that Orwyle would suggest something so bloodthirsty, Rhaenyra insists otherwise and, after reminding Orwyle to bring the correspondence between Otto and Ormund for her inspection, and asking if there has been any word from Daemon regarding his embassy to Lady Jeyne Arryn, to which Orwyle responds there has not, takes her leave. Some time later, Rhaenyra meets Orwyle in the Small Council chamber: Orwyle informs her that while Otto wrote numerous letters to his nephew, Ormund never replied to any of them. When Rhaenyra questions why, Orwyle speculates Ormund ruled Oldtown as his own private kingdom and saw no need to engage with the rest of the realm. They are interrupted by Ulf White, who begins petioning Rhaenyra for favors from the crown for his drinking partners. Rhaenyra flatly refuses, annoyed he would waste her time with such frivolous requests, and bans him from frequenting taverns in Flea Bottom as the risk of a Green assassin killing him and depriving her of a dragon rider while he does so is too great. Disappointed, Ulf informs Rhaenyra that slanderous graffiti dubbing her "Queen of Bastards" is being scrawled on the walls of King's Landing's streets: Rhaenyra summons Ser Luthor Largent and instructs him to find and deal with the culprits. Rhaenyra presides over an evening meeting of the Small Council that is interrupted by Daemon's return from the Vale of Arryn : he places a charred skull in the centre of the table, proclaiming it the head of Sheepstealer 's rider. As Mysaria and Daemon argue over whether the gold Daemon received from Lady Jeyne Arryn should be used to help the smallfolk or pay the gold cloaks their outstanding wages, Rhaenyra, who has been staring unseeingly at the skull, orders the room cleared. Once she and Daemon are alone, she demands an explanation as to who Sheepstealer's rider was, whether he was allied with Aemond or Ormund, and how he managed to tame a wild dragon in the first place. Daemon admits he wasn't able to get those answers before killing the man, and Sheepstealer flew off into the wild afterwards, so they need no longer worry about him. Rhaenyra is displeased, indicating she wanted Sheepstealer's rider brought to her alive, with the heavy implication she wanted to personally kill him for his part in Jace's death. Daemon insists such an act wouldn't have satisfied her or ended her grief over her son's death, and that his way was better. Rhaenyra urges Daemon to tell the gold cloaks to be patient a little longer regarding their overdue pay, as she plans to use Lady Arryn's gold to help the smallfolk, and begrudgingly thanks him for avenging Jace before taking her leave to inform Alicent she has despatched men to take Otto's remains back to Oldtown per Alicent's request to bury him there. A few days later, Rhaenyra meets with Lady Sabitha Frey , who has come to court to complain that Rhaenyra is offering Harrenhal as a reward to anyone who kills Aemond for her, in spite of Jacaerys having previously promised House Frey the castle as payment for letting the Winter Wolves cross the Trident at the Twins . Rhaenyra offers Sabitha a seat on the Small Council as recompense, but Sabitha makes it clear she expects the crown to honor its word and give Harrenhal to the Freys in due course. The following Small Council meeting (which is overrun with cats brought in to control the rat infestation) is a fiasco: Addam and Baela report Vhagar has been sighted attacking farms near Wendish Town , Daemon informs them of public disturbances in King's Landing, including the murder of two gold cloaks in Flea Bottom, and Orwyle reports that Criston Cole and his forces are harrying Oscar Tully and Roderick Dustin's army, delaying their march to Tumbleton. Rhaenyra is fixated on Aemond and Vhagar, ordering Daemon to hunt them down when Addam insists he, Baela and their dragons need to rest before they head out again. Daemon refuses, however, insisting on getting to the bottom of who is killing his men of the City Watch. Rhaenyra adjourns the meeting to speak with Daemon privately, accusing him of undermining her again. Daemon argues that Rhaenyra's fixation on Aemond and Vhagar is motivated more by her desire for revenge for Lucerys than fear of any threat the pair pose to her rule, as well as rebuking her for ordering Luthor and his men to be so heavy handed over graffiti mocking her, which he believes is what trigged the killings. Rhaenyra rages that such graffiti is an insult to her and her sons' legitimacy: Daemon insists her command of so many dragons is all the legitimacy she needs. They are interrupted by Elinda Massey , who informs Rhaenyra that her son Joffrey has arrived from the Vale and is asking to see her. Rhaenyra demurs, saying she will go to her son when she is able. Rhaenyra later goes to the Grand Sept to pray, much to Daemon's amusement when he finds her there: conversing in High Valyrian so the septons and septas present cannot eavesdrop, Daemon reports six gold cloaks have been murdered, and he suspects there is someone masterminding the attacks to undermine their rule. Rhaenyra bemoans that the gods have seemingly turned against her, but Daemon reminds her as a woman aspiring to rule, there would always be those who opposed her solely for that. Rhaenyra refuses to be appeased, however, and accuses Daemon of being outmaneuvered by their enemies. That evening, however, as Rhaenyra and Alyn discuss rebuilding the Velaryon fleet, Daemon interrupts them with the identity of the mastermind behind the disorder in the city: Ormund Hightower, who is financing insurrection within King's Landing with the goal of deposing Rhaenyra and placing Daeron upon the Iron Throne. At another Small Council meeting several days later, following the murders of Ser Luthor Largent and several senior officers of the gold cloaks, a furious Daemon demands retaliation against Ormund at Tumbleton: when Orwyle reports Lords Tully and Dustin have been delayed by Criston Cole, Daemon argues that the town should be razed to the ground to wipe out Ormund and his army. The rest of the Small Council balk at such a plan which will kill hundreds of Rhaenyra's loyal subjects: Rhaenyra vetoes Daemon's demand but agrees to send assassins to kill Ormund and Daeron for fomenting insurrection in King's Landing. Daemon insists on commanding the assassins, but Rhaenyra insists he is too recognizable for such subterfuge, instead charging him with rooting out the rest of Ormund's loyalists in the city. Alyn of Hull offers the service of House Velaryon's men at arms in King's Landing, but Daemon refuses him: Rhaenyra in turn requests Alyn petition Lord Corlys for more Velaryon soldiers to aid the gold cloaks in maintaining law and order in the city. As Orwyle asks who she will send to Tumbleton, Ser Lyonel Bentley of the Queensguard informs Rhaenyra that a delegation from House Baratheon has arrived. Rhaenyra goes to meet with the Baratheon envoys, discovering to her fury that despite her summons, Lord Borros Baratheon has sent his cousin, Ser Arrion Baratheon in his stead. When Rhaenyra demands an explanation, Arrion explains that Borros has taken his army into the Red Mountains to deal with a Dornish bandit calling himself the Vulture King , whose forces have been raiding the Stormlands . Enraged by this latest insult in addition to Borros's complicity in her son Lucerys's death , Rhaenyra threatens to declare Borros a traitor for his defiance and hang Arrion in his place. A rattled Arrion pleads for more time on Borros's behalf and offers to provide any other service Rhaenyra desires in compensation for the delay: sensing an opportunity, Rhaenyra orders Arrion and his retinue to surrender their attire, intending to pass her assassins off as Baratheon envoys to Ormund. Rhaenyra goes next to confront Alicent and Helaena, who were caught trying to escape the Red Keep via the secret passages. Rhaenyra begins berating Alicent for her lack of gratitude in sparing her and Helaena's lives when many had advised Rhaenyra to simply execute the pair of them when she took King's Landing, when Alicent confesses Helaena is pregnant, and the escape was done with the intent of protecting Helaena and her unborn child from being either killed as a threat to Rhaenyra's rule or used as bargaining chips against her enemies. Alicent insists she will accept any punishment Rhaenyra deems fit but pleads with her not to punish Helaena, who won't be able to cope with stricter imprisonment. Rhaenyra refuses, insisting she has no choice but to confine Helaena more tightly to prevent her pregnancy becoming common knowledge, as she will be forced to kill her half-sister if word gets out Helaena is carrying Aegon's child. Alicent suggests sending herself and Helaena into exile, but Rhaenyra will not hear of it, as in the eyes of her court, showing such mercy to a woman they deem Rhaenyra's enemy while Aemond and Ormund are still running amok will be construed as weakness. Alicent quietly asks if Rhaenyra considers her an enemy: Rhaenyra coldly warns Alicent not to try her patience again before leaving. Outside Alicent's chambers, Rhaenyra questions Mysaria if she knew about Helaena's pregnancy: Mysaria denies any knowledge. Rhaenyra later sits the Iron Throne and hold court, but the complaints of the petitioners, and their refusal to accept her explanation that Ormund Hightower is at the root of their woes, only enflame her already foul mood, and she storms out of the session. That evening, Alicent is brought to her chambers, offering knowledge of Aemond's whereabouts in return for her and Helaena's freedom. Rhaenyra initially dismisses Alicent, but grows more interested when she realizes from Alicent's description that Helaena is a dreamer , and that she has seen Aemond at Harrenhal, abandoned by Vhagar. Realizing that without Vhagar, Aemond is vulnerable, and killing him eliminates one of the greatest threats to her rule, Rhaenyra orders Alicent to go to Harrenhal and kill Aemond, as she fears he will go to ground if she sends assassins, but he might let his guard down around his mother. Alicent is appalled at this ultimatum, but Rhaenyra obliquely implies that she will harm Helaena and her unborn child if Alicent refuses. That night, Orwyle presents Rhaenyra with a bloodied Baratheon surcoat from Tumbleton, a message from Ormund that her attempt on his life has failed. A few days later, Rhaenyra goes to Helaena's room and wakes her half-sister from sleep to speak with her. She asks Helaena why she didn't ride Dreamfyre into battle alongside Aemond, as Lord Corlys suspected she would. Helaena replies she found dragon riding too overwhelming, and speculates that she, and their father believed close proximity to the creatures changes the Targaryens for the worse. Rhaenyra dismisses the idea, then relates to Helaena the possibility she is a dreamer, and presses her whether she has seen Daemon and the Winter Wolves victorious at Tumbleton. Helaena insists her abilities do not work that way, that she only sees glimpses of possibilities, but Rhaenyra assumes Helaena is lying or deliberately withholding information from her, and demands Helaena tell her she has seen some sign that Rhaenyra's victory is inevitable. At another Small Council meeting later on, Rhaenyra endures Torrhen's complaints and accusations that she is using him as a scapegoat to direct the smallfolk's anger towards over King's Landing's dire financial situation, and that his suggestions on how to raise funds to alleviate that are being ignored. She dismisses him and ask Orwyle if there is word from Corlys or Daemon: Orwyle answers that according to the Dragonkeepers, Daemon left the city with Caraxes at dawn on an unknown errand. When Lady Sabitha asks what is to be done with Harrenhal once Aemond has been eliminated, an annoyed Rhaenyra tells her to just take the castle. A delighted Sabitha agrees to the queen's command to return to the Twins to gather her soldiers and take and hold Harrenhal, as even if the assassination attempt fails and Aemond flees, it will ensure he cannot take shelter in the castle if he attempts to return. The meeting is interrupted by Baela and Addam, who report they have seen Sheepstealer flying in the Riverlands, with a new rider. Rhaenyra adjourns the meeting: as she leaves, Mysaria warns her that she suspects Daemon and Sheepstealer's rider are in cahoots, and that Daemon is plotting to undermine her out of dissatisfaction with her rule. Rhaenyra is reluctant to believe Daemon would go behind her back, but Mysaria asks her, given they both know what Daemon is capable of , if she truly believe it is beyond Daemon to deceive her. Rhaenyra mounts Syrax , and accompanied by Addam on Seasmoke , journeys to the Riverlands, where she is shocked to discover Sheepstealer's rider is Daemon's younger daughter, Rhaena Targaryen . She angrily demands to know if Daemon, who is also present, having located and tried to persuade his daughter to accept his help, knew the truth, but Sheepstealer, angry at being seperated from his rider, attacks them; Daemon orders Addam to get Rhaenyra and Rhaena to safety while he and Caraxes stay behind to fight off Sheepstealer. Rhaenyra takes Rhaena back to the Red Keep and orders her confined to a room. When Daemon returns to King's Landing, he tries to explain his actions, insisting he only lied out of concern for his daughter's safety: Rhaenyra angrily asks him if he thought she would have killed Rhaena for what happened at the Gullet, and sends him away before tossing the purported skull of Jace's killer he gave her into the fireplace. Mysaria comes to her chambers soon after: Rhaenyra accuses Mysaria of trying to turn her against Daemon, but Mysaria insists she has only advised Rhaenyra on how best to rule following Viserys's example. Rhaenyra bitterly laments that doing so has won her nothing, but Mysaria reassures her that soon enough she will emerge triumphant, and that she still believes Rhaenyra is worthy to rule. Mollified by this, Rhaenyra has sex with Mysaria. A few days later, a panic-stricken Rhaenyra bursts into Daemon's chambers as he dons his armor to join the Black army about to attack Tumbleton, alerting him to Aegon and Sunfyre 's apparent resurrection and destruction of Lord Walys Mooton 's army near Rook's Rest and that the commonfolk are apparently taking it as a sign from the gods Aegon is ordained to rule. Ordering his squires out, Daemon reassures his panicking wife that as the blood of Old Valyria, they need not concern themselves with 'lesser gods', reminding her that the realm only respects strength. Calming down at her husband's reassurance, Rhaenyra instructs Daemon to proceed with the attack on Tumbleton and kill every last Hightower within its walls, though she caveats he is to minimize civilian loss of life in retaking Tumbleton to avoid turning the realm against her. As Rhaenyra leaves Daemon's chambers, she is accosted by Baela, who demands to know if plans have been to rescue Corlys. Rhaenyra answers that Daemon and his troops will scour Tumbleton for Corlys once the town is retaken: Baela protests that Corlys will likely be dead by then (either killed in the fighting or executed by the Hightowers to prevent his rescue) and begs that she be allowed to lead a rescue mission now. Rhaenyra refuses, insisting Baela and Moondancer are needed alongside Addam and Seasmoke to defend King's Landing in the event the rumors of Sunfyre's survival are true (her tone indicating she blames Baela for not noticing any signs of life from Sunfyre on her previous sorties near Rook's Rest). Baela blames Rhaenyra for driving Corlys away and leaving him at risk of being taken prisoner by Ormund Hightower's forces, accusing her of mistreating those who serve her loyally and abandoning those who fail or are of no futher use to her, like she has Corlys and Rhaena. Rhaenyra coldly retorts she would have been justified in abandoning Baela after her involvement in Jace's death at the Battle of the Gullet: Baela agrees, but points out Rhaenyra still needs her dragon. An angered Rhaenyra grabs Baela's face and hisses that she is an insolent child, before bitterly admitting she cannot  truly blame her for it: Baela and Rhaena are both Daemon's daughters, and "insolence runs in [their] blood." Rhaenyra is then informed by Elinda Massey that Helaena is refusing to eat, and the maesters fear for her well-being and that of her unborn child as a result. Rhaenyra requests Elinda summon Alyn of Hull to assemble his men to escort her to the Grand Sept : she intends to force the High Septon to annoint her as Queen and bless her reign in the eyes of the Seven. She also despatches Elinda to convey a message to Mysaria that she is relieved of her position and is to leave King's Landing for Pentos by ship that day. She then goes to Helaena's chambers and urges her half-sister to eat, if only for the sake of her child. Helaena refuses, outright telling Rhaenyra Viserys would hate the person she has become, and calling Rhaenyra and her ambitions for power "ugly". Angered by the rebuke, Rhaenyra orders Helaena to eat: when she refuses again, Rhaenyra orders the guards to force feed Helaena. Rhaenyra then dons a suit of armor and her crown, and departs for the Grand Sept accompanied by her son, Prince Joffrey Velaryon , Alyn of Hull and an escort of Targaryen and Velaryon guardsmen. On route, she tells Joffrey, as he is now her heir, of The Song of Ice and Fire . Upon their arrival at the Grand Sept, Rhaenyra and her men force their way inside: the High Septon protests her bringing armed soldiers into the sept, but Rhaenyra ignores his complaints and demands he annoint her as queen before all the people of King's Landing gathered outside the sept. The High Septon refuses, reminding her of the reasons he previously cited, and calling Aegon's seeming resurrection a clear sign from the Seven who is chosen to rule. Angered by him referring to her as "Princess" rather than "Queen", Rhaenyra reminds the High Septon she possesses the crown, the Iron Throne and six dragons, inferring there will be fatal consequences if he refuses her again. The High Septon retorts that while she may have six dragons, he cannot deny the will of the Seven. Rhaenyra scornfully replies the High Septon merely names himself a traitor and orders Alyn to execute him. Though Alyn is briefly given pause when the High Septon threatens him with eternal damnation if he obeys, Rhaenyra reassures Alyn that, as the blood of Old Valyria , they do not answer to the lesser gods of the Andals, mocking the Grand Sept as "an empty work of brick and stone" before leading Joffrey outside as Alyn carries out the High Septon's execution. Outside the Grand Sept, Rhaenyra then, ranting in High Valyrian , proclaims herself the Prince Who Was Promised, destined to save the world of Men from the return of the Long Night , to the indifference of the crowd and the concern of her advisors (Orwyle, Torrhen and Alyn on the steps beside her, Mysaria hidden in the crowd) at Rhaenyra's increasingly unhinged state of mind. Upon her return to the Red Keep, Rhaenyra is informed by Elinda that Helaena has committed suicide to escape her captivity. Making for Helaena's chambers, she finds the window open where Helaena flung herself from it, and a tapestry her half-sister was sewing, depicting herself seated upon the Iron Throne, a sword in hand, surrounded by blood and flames. Biography [ ] Background [ ] Rhaenys Targaryen rode the dragon Meraxes Rhaenys and her siblings on Dragonstone Rhaenys was the sister of Aegon and Visenya , and was born on Dragonstone , the Targaryen stronghold in the Narrow Sea . [citation needed] Following Valyrian custom, she and Visenya both married Aegon. All three rode dragons , and Rhaenys rode the one named Meraxes . During Aegon's Conquest , she rode her dragon at the Field of Fire , where the Targaryens destroyed the largest army ever fielded against their troops and broke the bulk of resistance to their rule in Westeros . However, Rhaenys ultimately perished along with her dragon in her attempt to conquer Dorne . Game of Thrones : Season 2 [ ] Arya Stark , while posing as a common serving girl in Lannister -occupied Harrenhal, discusses the razing of the castle with Lord Tywin Lannister . She mentions Rhaenys and her dragon, but admits that Visenya was more of a hero of hers. ↑ Histories & Lore : Season 1 , Short 24: " House Targaryen " (2012). ↑ Game of Thrones: Conquest & Rebellion: An Animated History of the Seven Kingdoms , Chapter 9: " House Martell, Princes of Dorne " (2017). ↑ 3.0 3.1 Game of Thrones : Season 2 , Episode 7: " A Man Without Honor " (2012). ↑ Histories & Lore : Season 5 , Short 9: " Dorne " (2016).

Biography [ ] Background [ ] Rickard Karstark is the Lord of Karhold and the head of House Karstark , a vassal family to House Stark of Winterfell . He is a close ally and distant relation of House Stark. He has three sons, Torrhen Karstark , Harrion Karstark , and Harald Karstark , and one granddaughter, Alys Karstark . Game of Thrones : Season 1 [ ] Lord Karstark listens to the debate between Robb , Jonos Bracken and Greatjon Umber about whether they should join forces with Renly or Stannis . When the Greatjon names Robb as the King in the North and lays his sword at his feet, Rickard is the second to join him, saying he'll have peace on those terms. Game of Thrones : Season 2 [ ] Rickard listens as Alton Lannister delivers the Queen's response to their peace terms. Rickard Karstark is among Robb's host in the Westerlands and is present when Alton Lannister gives Cersei 's response to Robb's peace terms, including the independence of the North, which she rejects. Karstark's son Torrhen is later killed by Jaime during an escape attempt. After Jaime's recapture, Rickard demands Jaime's execution in revenge for the murder of his son, but Catelyn speaks for his life. Rickard argues with Catelyn. After Lord Rickard's threatening reaction, she reminds him that he has sworn an oath of loyalty to Robb and that Jaime is a prisoner of war. She says that he should remember who his king is and who she is. She promises him that Jaime will be punished for what he did. Reluctantly Lord Karstark gives in, but demands retribution when his King returns from the Crag . During the confrontation with Lady Catelyn, Lord Rickard also dismisses Talisa as a "foreign bitch". An angered Rickard confronts Catelyn. Catelyn sends Jaime to King's Landing with her sworn sword Brienne to exchange him for her captive daughters, fearing that Rickard or his men will kill him if he remains in the camp. He is furious that she has denied him his vengeance and rejects her argument that Jaime may yet save the lives of her children, adding that he personally would happily exchange his life for those of his deceased children, Torrhen and Harrion, even if it meant captivity for them. Robb tells Catelyn that she has betrayed him and orders her kept under guard. Game of Thrones : Season 3 [ ] Rickard and Roose Bolton find the slaughtered prisoners at Harrenhal. Rickard's faith in Robb continues to deteriorate as the Northern host arrives at Harrenhal , finding the castle's inhabitants had been put to the sword . Roose Bolton attempts to reassure Rickard, telling him that he has sent his best hunter in pursuit of Jaime, and that the dead will be avenged in time. Karstark, however, is clearly unconvinced, losing confidence in Robb's sense of leadership and the possibility of a Northern victory. Rickard and Robb discuss the movement of troops to Riverrun. Lord Karstark manifests his disapproval of the march to Riverrun for the funeral of Hoster Tully , considering it a distraction from the war effort. When questioned by Robb if he has lost faith in the Northern cause, Lord Karstark insists that if the cause is revenge he will keep faith "until it snows in Dorne ", but adds that he believes Robb lost the war the day he married Talisa, a political nobody with no influence in Westeros. Rickard and his men kill Martyn and Willem Lannister in the dungeons of Riverrun and are brought before Robb Stark. He openly insults the King in the North and claims the war is a lost cause. Remaining true to his honor just like his father, Robb decides that Lord Karstark must die for his treason. Though Edmure , Talisa, and Catelyn attempt to advise Robb to hold Karstark hostage and send him to the Night's Watch after the war - on the basis that the Karstarks form a significant portion of Robb's army, and they will abandon Robb if he executes their lord. Despite the warnings of all of his councilors, Robb refuses to listen. Rickard is executed for treason by Robb. Before he is executed, Karstark reminds Robb that the blood of the First Men run through both of their veins; that he fought alongside Eddard during Robert's Rebellion and alongside Robb himself against Joffrey; finally, he states that they are both kin, since House Karstark was founded by Karlon Stark . Robb tells him that all of it didn't stop him from murdering the Lannister boys and it will not save him now. Rickard states contemptuously that he does not want to be saved, but he wants it to haunt him for the rest of his days. True to the traditions of the North and his father, Robb personally beheads Karstark with a single strike of his sword after Rickard curses Robb and renounces all allegiance to him. In the aftermath, the Karstark forces abandon Robb and return home. In the meantime, while he is being tortured in the Dreadfort , Theon incorrectly assumes Ramsay Snow to be Rickard's son, keeping him prisoner on Rickard's orders, since he is Robb's bannerman, remaining unaware that Rickard has been executed. Game of Thrones : Season 6 [ ] Rickard is mentioned by his last living son Harald when he meets with the Boltons at Winterfell. Harald makes it clear that his House will never support the Starks again after Robb executed his father. Despite the fact that Roose avenged his father by killing Robb at the Red Wedding , Harald makes no attempt to intervene when Ramsay kills Roose after the birth of his half-brother , whom Ramsay also murders along with his stepmother, Walda Bolton . While planning to counter the Boltons' claim to the North, Sansa expresses her belief that the Karstarks will support them when they learn of Jon 's resurrection, but Davos reminds her that Rickard was executed by Robb, which is likely why Rickard's last surviving son has sided with the Starks' enemies and not out of ignorance as Sansa had hoped. ↑ HBO viewers guide, season 2 guide to houses, House Stark - Rickard Karstark entry ↑ 2.0 2.1 2.2 Game of Thrones : Season 2 , Episode 7: " A Man Without Honor " (2012). ↑ 3.0 3.1 3.2 3.3 Game of Thrones : Season 3 , Episode 5: " Kissed by Fire " (2013). ↑ Game of Thrones : Season 7 , Episode 1: " Dragonstone " (2017). ↑ Game of Thrones : Season 1 , Episode 10: " Fire and Blood " (2011). ↑ Game of Thrones : Season 2 , Episode 8: " The Prince of Winterfell " (2012). ↑ Game of Thrones : Season 3 , Episode 1: " Valar Dohaeris " (2013). ↑ Game of Thrones : Season 3 , Episode 2: " Dark Wings, Dark Words " (2013). ↑ Game of Thrones : Season 3 , Episode 6: " The Climb " (2013). ↑ Game of Thrones : Season 6 , Episode 2: " Home " (2016). ↑ Game of Thrones : Season 6 , Episode 5: " The Door " (2016).

Biography [ ] Background [ ] Rickard and Brandon are arrested by Targaryen guards. Rickard is burned alive with wildfire by the Mad King. Rickard Stark was the head of House Stark and Warden of the North . He served under King Aerys II (known as the Mad King). He was saved from drowning by Ser Gwayne Gaunt during the siege of White Harbor by the outlaw Sea Kings . Rickard is the father of Brandon , Eddard , Lyanna and Benjen Stark . He arranged for the betrothal of his daughter Lyanna to Robert Baratheon , the Lord of the Stormlands . He also betrothed his son and heir Brandon to Catelyn , the daughter of Hoster Tully , Lord Paramount of the Trident . Both engagements were broken when Prince Rhaegar Targaryen allegedly abducted Lyanna. [citation needed] When Lyanna was kidnapped by Rhaegar, Rickard's eldest son and heir, Brandon, rode to King's Landing seeking justice. Aerys imprisoned Brandon and ordered that Rickard ride south to answer for his son's impertinence. Against advice, Rickard agreed, assuming that the matter would be settled through a trial or a bargain of some kind. Instead, Aerys had Rickard burned alive while Brandon strangled himself trying to save his father. Aerys then ordered Jon Arryn to hand over his ward and new Lord of Winterfell Eddard Stark. Having sworn a sacred oath to protect Eddard, Jon instead rose his banners in rebellion. He was supported by the North, Lyanna's betrothed Robert, and Hoster Tully. This sparked the beginning of the war known as Robert's Rebellion , which led to the near-destruction of House Targaryen and its removal from the Iron Throne . Game of Thrones : Season 1 [ ] Reaching King's Landing, Eddard is greeted by Jaime in the throne room, who recalls listening to Eddard's father and brother scream as hundreds watched them die at the whim of the Mad King. He suggests his assassination of the Mad King was an act of justice, but Eddard dismisses that as a paltry self-justification for breaking his solemn Kingsguard vows. Game of Thrones : Season 5 [ ] Barristan Selmy vaguely alludes to Rickard and his son Brandon's deaths when he tells her about how her father murdered sons in front of their fathers and how his actions led to a rebellion that killed every Targaryen, save for Daenerys and her other brother Viserys , who has also since died. Later, when Tyrion is advising Daenerys about her strategy of reclaiming the Iron Throne, he points out her lack of support by the Great Houses. As he lists them, he reminds her that House Stark is gone due to the actions of their "two terrible fathers" though he doesn't discuss the specifics - her father executing Rickard and Brandon and his father orchestrating the Red Wedding . Game of Thrones : Season 6 [ ] Bran , with the aid of Brynden Rivers , has a vision of Lord Rickard giving some parting words to the young Ned Stark as he prepares to leave Winterfell to be fostered in the Eyrie . Rickard advises his son to comport himself with dignity and stay out of fights, but implores him to win if he must fight. Seeing and hearing his grandfather for the first time brings a smile to Bran's face. Game of Thrones : Season 7 [ ] When Jon Snow agrees to meet with Daenerys to discuss an alliance, Sansa angrily reminds him what Daenerys's father did to their grandfather. Jon refuses to bend the knee to Daenerys, reminding her of how her father executed his grandfather and uncle. Daenerys admits that her father was an evil man and asks forgiveness for the crimes he committed against House Stark. After the execution of Randyll and Dickon Tarly , following the Battle of the Goldroad , Varys compares Daenerys to Aerys, as he did the same with Rickard and Brandon. Varys then implores Tyrion to make her listen, fearing that this will make her be viewed in a similar vision to her father. Biography [ ] Background [ ] Rickon is the fifth child and youngest son of Lady Catelyn and Lord Eddard Stark . Eddard is the head of House Stark . The North is one of the constituent regions of the Seven Kingdoms and House Stark is one of the Great Houses of the realm. House Stark rules the region from their seat of Winterfell while Eddard holds the title of Lord of Winterfell . He is also the Warden of the North to King Robert Baratheon . Rickon was born and raised at Winterfell. He has two older brothers, Robb and Bran , and two older sisters, Sansa and Arya . He also has an older "bastard half-brother", Jon Snow . He is six-years-old when his uncle, Lord Jon Arryn , the Hand of the King , mysteriously dies. Game of Thrones : Season 1 [ ] Rickon watches Bran's archery training. Rickon watches Bran's unsuccessful practice at archery and laughs when Bran misses and is outwitted by Arya; Rickon later helps Robb and Jon put the arrows back in their place. His brothers find a litter of direwolf pups in the Wolfswood and bring them back to Winterfell. Rickon adopts one of the pups and names him Shaggydog . Rickon receives the visiting King Robert Baratheon with his family at Winterfell , standing close to his mother. During the welcome, Robert fondly ruffles his hair. His father accepts Robert's offer to serve as the Hand of the King . Rickon's brother, Bran, is found severely injured at the base of a disused tower. Eddard travels south to the capital King's Landing , taking Arya and Sansa with him. Catelyn initially remains with Bran, but after protecting him from an assassination attempt and then discovering evidence implicating House Lannister in his injuries, she follows Eddard south to warn him in secret. Rickon's oldest brother, Robb , is left in charge of Winterfell. King Robert dies as a result of a hunting accident . His son Joffrey Baratheon claims the throne. Eddard challenges his legitimacy and is arrested for treason. Robb decides to ride against King Joffrey and wants to bid his younger brothers goodbye, but Rickon is nowhere to be found. Afterwards, Bran tries to reassure Rickon that Robb will return along with their parents, but Rickon wistfully replies, "No, they won't." Rickon ventures in crypts with Shaggydog. Rickon sees his father in the crypts below Winterfell in a dream . He goes down to the crypts with Shaggydog to look for him. He meets Bran, who also had a dream about his father being there. When Bran emerges from the crypts, Maester Luwin tells him that their father has been killed for treason against Joffrey Baratheon . Game of Thrones : Season 2 [ ] Rickon resentfully shells nuts. As Bran holds court for his people, remaining the the acting Lord of Winterfell, Rickon sits beside his older brother, shelling nuts loudly with a rock. A shepherd reports being unable to tend to his flock with his three sons fighting in the south and Bran offers to assign two orphans from Winterfell's outlying winter town to aid him if he will give them room and board. The shepherd gratefully accepts. When the shepherd leaves, Bran tells Rickon to stop. Having seen everyone, Bran tells Maester Luwin that he is going to go for a ride before dark and calls for Hodor . Rickon witnesses Rodrik's execution. An attack on Torrhen's Square is used as a feint orchestrated by Theon Greyjoy to lure away the garrison, headed by Rodrik Cassel , from Winterfell. He seizes the poorly defended castle and forces Bran to surrender to him by threatening the people. Rickon is distraught when Theon publicly executes Rodrik. Along with Bran, he tries to plead for Rodrik's life but to no avail. Osha manages to free Bran and Rickon and leads them out of the castle. They reach the shepherd's farm in the winter town. Rickon remembers that Bran sent Billy and Jack there and wants to approach them for food. Bran is cautious about putting them in danger if they are tracked. Rickon is revealed to be alive. Bran's concern proves valid when Theon later reaches the farm but cannot find Bran or Rickon. He brutalizes the shepherd and then returns to Winterfell with the charred corpses of two boys, claiming that they are Bran and Rickon. The escapees actually back tracked through the stream and are hiding in the crypts at Winterfell. Luwin correctly deduces that the bodies must be the orphans from the farm. A Bolton force led by Roose 's bastard son, Ramsay Snow , besieges Winterfell, trapping Theon's meager Ironborn garrison. The Ironborn turn on Theon and accept Robb Stark's offer to spare their lives in return for surrendering. However, the House Bolton forces flay the Ironborn alive and sacks Winterfell, killing many of its inhabitants in the process. Rickon and Shaggydog leave Winterfell with Bran, Osha, Hodor and Summer. Following the Sack of Winterfell , Rickon and his companions emerge from the crypt to discover Winterfell in ruins. They also find a dying Maester Luwin resting under the willow tree. While Bran and Rickon offer to bring medicine to treat Luwin's wounds, he declines their offer and tells them to gather all of their warm clothing and travel north to Castle Black , where they would be safe with their half-brother, Jon Snow. At Luwin's own request, Osha euthanizes the elderly maester after the boys leave with Hodor. Rickon then travels north, accompanied by his older brother, Bran; their guardian, Osha; Hodor; and their two direwolves. Game of Thrones : Season 3 [ ] Rickon is startled when his brother wakes up from a vision. Following the capture of Winterfell , Rickon, along with Bran, Osha, Hodor, and the direwolves, Summer and Shaggydog, travel north toward Castle Black, the headquarters of the Night's Watch . Rickon inquires into Bran's welfare following his awakening from a vision . During the journey, the group encounters Jojen Reed and his sister, Meera Reed . During the first encounter between the two parties, Rickon and Hodor are out hunting, leaving Bran and Osha behind to guard the camp. The siblings are members of House Reed , a vassal house of House Stark , and had been searching for Bran and Rickon so that they can protect them. Bran also experiences strange dreams of seeing the world through the eyes of his wolf, Summer. Bran would later learn from Jojen that he is a warg and has the ability to enter the minds of animals and control their actions. On one occasion, Rickon is present when Jojen descends into a fit due to the exertions of his vision. Rickon and the group arrive at Queenscrown. Later, Rickon and his companions reach the Gift , a region south of the Wall that is considered to be beyond the borders of the Seven Kingdoms. The Gift had been granted to the Night's Watch thousands of years ago by Brandon the Builder , from which the Watch draws support for its material needs. While the region is fertile, it has become uninhabited due to frequent wildling attacks that forced the smallfolk to migrate south over the centuries. When his brother, Bran, raises this controversial issue, which troubles Osha due to her Wildling ancestry, Rickon adds that he had heard tales about the Wildlings drinking blood. Rickon is shocked when his brother wargs into Hodor. Rickon and his companions take shelter at an abandoned mill to escape a thunderstorm. Later, the group notices a band of Wildlings chasing down a Northman. During the ensuing incident, Bran uses his Warg powers to Warg through Summer and Shaggydog to fight off the Wildlings. This party of Wildlings includes Jon Snow , who earlier had been taken captive by them. Using his Warg abilities, Bran helps Jon Snow escape from his captors and later return to the Night's Watch. Rickon is comforted by Osha before their departure. Following the events of that night, Bran instructs Osha to bring Rickon to Last Hearth , the seat of House Umber , whose lord, Jon Umber , was a loyal bannerman of the Starks. This arrangement also suited Osha because she was unwilling to travel beyond the Wall with Bran due to the threat of the White Walkers . Rickon becomes upset, being separated from his brother and expresses his desire to accompany him on his journey. Bran tells him that if he or Robb do not return, Rickon needs to stay alive as the heir to Winterfell. Accompanied by his direwolf, Shaggydog, Rickon leaves with Osha as they head for the Last Hearth. It is around this time that the Red Wedding takes place and several more members of Rickon's family are killed: his mother, Catelyn Stark; his brother, Robb Stark; his pregnant sister-in-law, Talisa ; and her unborn child. Game of Thrones : Season 4 [ ] After the Red Wedding, the Starks' former bannerman, Roose Bolton , who personally killed Robb, is appointed as the new Warden of the North. His bastard son, Ramsay Snow , has physically and psychologically tortured Theon Greyjoy , the Starks' former ward, turning him into a broken pet called "Reek", who reveals to Roose that he did not in fact kill Bran and Rickon, and that they may be with Jon Snow at the Wall . Roose sends his best hunter, Locke , to find Bran and Rickon, promising him a 1000 acres and a holdfast. Locke infiltrates the Night's Watch and eventually catches up with Bran at Craster's Keep , but Bran wargs into Hodor and kills Locke before he can interrogate him as to Rickon's whereabouts. After the Bolton army drives the remaining Ironborn from the North and takes Winterfell, Roose Bolton asks Ramsay if he has heard anything from Locke. Ramsay informs him that he has not. Roose dismisses Locke's absence as unimportant, speculating that Bran and Rickon may already be dead anyway. Game of Thrones : Season 5 [ ] Rickon is still largely believed to have died along with Bran at the hands of Theon. When Sansa Stark returns to Winterfell to be wed to Ramsay at the behest of Petyr Baelish , Ramsay initially forces Theon to keep up the charade and apologize to Sansa. Eventually, however, an irate Sansa forces Theon to finally admit that he did not kill her brothers. Stunned by this admission, her anger towards Theon cools but when she asks if he knows where they might have gone to, he breaks down and leaves the room, fearful of what Ramsay will do if and when he finds out what he just told her. However, Sansa appears to be left with a sense of renewed hope by the revelation that she still has surviving family left. Game of Thrones : Season 6 [ ] Rickon and Osha are presented to Ramsay Bolton by Smalljon Umber. Rickon and Osha, having reached Last Hearth, are betrayed by Smalljon Umber after the Greatjon's passing and brought before Ramsay Bolton in order to form an alliance against Jon Snow and the Wildlings. After seeing Shaggydog's decapitated head as proof of the boy's identity, Ramsay sarcastically welcomes Rickon home, while Rickon shows visible signs of anger at Ramsay and his dead direwolf. Jon and Sansa later receive a letter from Ramsay that says he has Rickon in his dungeon and that his hounds will kill their "wild little brother" if Sansa is not returned. After hearing that Rickon is in danger, Jon and Sansa declare war on Ramsay. In order to lure Jon Snow out, Ramsay uses Rickon as bait. Before they commence battle, the three of them have a parley where Ramsay asks Jon and Sansa if they will let Rickon die because they are too proud to surrender. When Sansa asks for proof that he actually has her brother, Smalljon pulls Shaggydog's head out of a sack and tosses it to the ground in front of them. Ramsay begins to repeat his terms if they wish to save Rickon but Sansa, having firsthand experience of Ramsay's "mercy", cuts him off and declares that he is going to die the next day. Rickon is killed by Ramsay. As the two armies face each other on the battlefield , Rickon is brought forward. He lowers his head as Ramsay raises a dagger, but his captor simply cuts the ropes and asks if Rickon likes games. He tells the boy to run to his brother. Rickon begins to walk but looks back to see Ramsay taunting him and starts running. Jon, knowing what Ramsay is plotting, begins riding towards Rickon who keeps running and is nearly hit as arrows land dangerously close. Just as Rickon is about to reach his brother, he is struck by an arrow and killed. This in turn provokes Jon and his army into attacking the Bolton forces while Rickon's body is hit with another volley of arrows. Jon orders his brother's burial. Though the battle proves costly to the Stark forces, they ultimately emerge victorious due to the arrival of a House Arryn cavalry force. Rickon is avenged when Smalljon is killed in battle by Tormund , and Ramsay is viciously beaten to a bloody pulp by Jon before being fed to his own hounds on Sansa's orders. After the battle, his corpse is brought to Winterfell and Jon orders him to be buried in the crypts next to his father. Game of Thrones : Season 7 [ ] During the meeting at Dragonstone , Daenerys tells Jon "You lost two brothers", referring to Robb and Rickon. After returning to Winterfell, Arya is reunited with Sansa in the crypts, where Sansa tells her that Bran has returned but fails to mention Rickon, leading Arya to the distressing truth of Rickon's
